newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia stocks mixed, Dow rise eclipsed by local news.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks mixed, Dow rise eclipsed by local news.

text.p: Asian stock markets were narrowly mixed on Thursday as local factors in many centres overshadowed a dramatic rise of nearly 93 points on Wall Street overnight.
News that U.S. tobacco executives were negotiating a settlement of massive health-related lawsuits against them pulled tobacco stocks -- and the overall market -- sharply higher.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended 92.71 points, or 1.41 percent, higher at 6,679.87.
However, not all news from the United States was viewed as encouraging.

A larger than expected rise in March U.S. industrial production and a sharp gain in capacity utilisation revived concerns the ecomony may be expanding too rapidly, which could lead the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates again.
This and concern over the property market led a cautious Hong Kong market, where the Hang Seng Index was 11.92 points, or 0.09 percent, higher at 12,593.23 by the midday break.

"Investors are taking a breather after yesterday's jump because the market's upside -- although it's there -- isn't unlimited," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities in Hong Kong.
Tokyo stocks also shrugged off the rise in the Dow as profit-taking hit blue chip stocks. The key Nikkei 225 average was off 62.21 points, or 0.35 percent, at 18,093.41 by 0600 GMT.

"The market is suffering from a lack of firm direction," said a strategist at a second-tier brokerage firm in Tokyo. "Blue chips are slowing down and investors are wondering what to buy next," he added.
Malaysian stocks followed the trend in New York due to a lack of direction from local factors. The Composite index was up 16.53 points, or 1.52 percent, to 1,104.31.

In the Philippines, however, stocks ended off 1.12 percent due to a sharp drop in the price of blue chip Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) in New York overnight and lingering concerns over the property sector.
PLDT said on Wednesday it was near agreement with AT&T Corp to cut the rates on international calls.

In Thailand, stocks dropped 14.40 points, or 2.01 percent, to 702.49, after a sharp drop in troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) when its shares resumed trading after an 11-month suspension. "Looking at the balance sheet of BBC last week and I don't see any value," one trader said.

Taiwan stocks closed lower as investors fled to the sidelines amid concern over a government plan to accelerate the sale of shares in state-run commercial banks. The govenment's move to add supply to the market was seen as a deliberate bid to cool the market's advance.
News of the plan overshadowed the rise on Wall Street and news that Beijing had approved six Taiwan shipping forms to sail directly across the Taiwan strait for the first time since 1949.
The weighted index ended 122.68 points, or 1.42 percent, lower at 8,492.10.
Elsewhere in Asia, Indonesian shares were up 5.106 points, or 0.81 percent, at 637.925.

Stocks in Singapore were little changed, with the 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index up 5.62 points, or 0.28 percent, at 2,045.81, while those in Australia were up 6.8 points, or 0.28 percent, at 2,413.2. New Zealand shares ended down 1.53 points at 2,252.01.
